doc-welcome.title: What is DocPilot?
doc-welcome.summary: Quick orientation: what this platform is, who it's for, and how it's organised.
doc-welcome.html:
1.0

What is DocPilot?

DocPilot is a multi-tenant documentation platform for product teams that need to ship the same reference material to internal staff, partners, and external customers — without spinning up a new site per audience.

You're reading the demo

This entire document is a DocPilot doc. Every component you see — callouts, code blocks, tables, tabs, accordions — is part of the reader. Open the CMS in the same workspace to see how an author would build this.

Who it's for

  • Studios and software vendors who publish player manuals, integration guides, back-office runbooks, and API references.
  • Operations teams who need versioned documentation tied to releases.
  • Account managers who hand a single URL to a partner and trust that the right audience sees the right view.

Three things to look at

  1. The reader (this page). Read-optimised, dark-mode-aware, side-rail TOC, hash-anchored sub-sections, full-text search.
  2. The CMS at /admin/v2/login. Tenants edit their own docs, sections, media, and translations.
  3. The multi-tenant root at /c/<slug>. Each company gets its own branded landing + assigned account-manager surface.

doc-welcome.title: Components at a glance
doc-welcome.summary: Callouts, tables, code blocks, figures — the building blocks the reader renders.
doc-welcome.html:
2.0

Components at a glance

Every section is hand-authored HTML that the reader styles consistently. Here are the building blocks.

Callouts

Info callout

Use for context, links, and side-notes that don't gate the rest of the section.

Warning callout

Use for behaviour that's easy to misuse or for state-machine edges with non-obvious consequences.

Danger callout

Use sparingly. Destructive operations, security-relevant assumptions, things that can corrupt data.

Tables

ComponentHTML tagWhen to use
Calloutdiv.callout.{info,warn,danger}Side-notes and warnings
Code blockpre > codeSnippets, configs, payloads
TabletableReference matrices, comparisons
Figurefigure > img + figcaptionScreenshots, diagrams

Code blocks

// JS
async function fetchDoc(slug) {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/v2/docs/${slug}`, { credentials: 'include' });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return res.json();
}

Inline UI tokens

For short labels that should look like a control: Manual, Save, Delete. Inline code reads cleanly inside paragraphs.

doc-welcome.title: Interactive components
doc-welcome.summary: Tabs and accordions for content that benefits from progressive disclosure.
doc-welcome.html:
3.0

Interactive components

The reader wires up tab strips and accordions in the page automatically — no JavaScript in your section HTML required.

Tabs

Reader vs CMS

Read-only, indexed by search, no auth required for public docs.

  • Hash-anchored sub-headings, TOC in the side-rail.
  • Dark mode toggle with per-session preference.
  • Full-text search via ⌘K.

Authoring surface for tenant-admins.

  • Documents, sections, media, translations, releases.
  • Permission matrix per role (admin / editor / reviewer / viewer / partner / TAM).
  • Audit log and revision history.

Accordions

How are sections stored?

Each section is a row in the sections table with an html column. The reader fetches them by document and renders inline. Authors edit raw HTML for now (a WYSIWYG layer is roadmap).

Can I version a doc?

Yes. Each release captures a snapshot of the document + sections + translations. Rollbacks restore the snapshot atomically.

How do translations work?

A localization-key inventory is generated from the source HTML. Each key gets a translation per language. The reader looks up the key by language at render time.

doc-welcome.title: Tenancy & auth
doc-welcome.summary: How companies, users, and the reader's auth gate fit together.
doc-welcome.html:
4.0

Tenancy & auth

Every doc is owned by a company. Every user belongs to a company. The reader checks the session before serving non-public docs.

ConceptWhere it livesNotes
Companycompanies tableOne per tenant. Owns docs, users, branding, audit log.
Userusers tableEmail + bcrypt password. Roles assigned per company.
SessionHttpOnly cookie dp_session7-day expiry, rotated on rotation events. SameSite=Lax.
Doc auth gateDocAuthGate wrapperRedirects unauthenticated traffic to the tenant landing.

Roles

  • admin — full control of the platform (superadmin only).
  • company-admin — full control inside their company.
  • editor — write docs, sections, media, translations.
  • reviewer — translation review only.
  • viewer — read access to internal docs.
  • partner / tam — external collaborators with scoped writes.
Cookies and TLS

The session cookie's Secure flag is gated on the env var DOCPILOT_COOKIE_SECURE. Leave it off when reaching the site over plain HTTP (the browser will drop the cookie otherwise). Flip it on once TLS is in front.

doc-welcome.title: Deploying DocPilot
doc-welcome.summary: What's in the repo, what's needed at deploy time, what survives a rebuild.
doc-welcome.html:
5.0

Deploying DocPilot

DocPilot ships as a single Node process backed by SQLite. The Dockerfile in the repo root builds the SPA, bundles the server, and exposes port 4179.

Anatomy

dist/                  # built Vite SPA (served by the Node process)
server/
  docpilot-server.mjs  # HTTP entry, API + static
  api-v2.mjs           # multi-tenant API (auth, RBAC, audit)
  auth.mjs             # sessions, bcrypt, rate limits
  db.mjs               # better-sqlite3 + schema.sql
  seed-on-boot.mjs     # idempotent first-boot tenant seed
  seed-state.json      # optional initial CMS state
content/               # tenant content (this directory)
  docs.json
  games.json
  media-assets.json
  custom-sections.json

Env vars

VariableDefaultPurpose
ADMIN_EMAILadmin@aviator-studio.localFirst-boot admin email
ADMIN_PASSWORDrequiredFirst-boot admin password; stored bcrypt-hashed
COMPANY_SLUGaviatorSlug for the seeded company
COMPANY_NAMEAviator StudioDisplay name for the seeded company
DOCPILOT_COOKIE_SECURE0Set to 1 when behind TLS
DOCPILOT_DATA_DIR./.docpilot-dataSQLite + media + state file root

Persistence

Mount a volume at /app/.docpilot-data. That directory holds the SQLite file, media uploads, the legacy state file, and the mutation log. Everything else is rebuildable.

See DEPLOY-AWS.md

The repo includes a step-by-step EC2 playbook. The same Docker image works on Fly.io, Railway, Render, or any host with a persistent disk and Node 20.

doc-welcome.title: Next steps
doc-welcome.summary: What to do next: customize the content, fork the platform, contribute back.
doc-welcome.html:
6.0

Next steps

Customize the content

Everything you've read in this document lives in content/custom-sections.json. Edit that file (and content/docs.json, games.json, media-assets.json) to replace the demo with your own product. The platform code under src/ and server/ stays untouched.

Fork the platform

Clone the public repo and customize the content:

git clone https://github.com/EarendilM83/DocPilot.git my-docs
cd my-docs
# edit content/*.json with your docs/games/sections
npm ci
npm run build
docker build -t my-docs .
docker run -d --restart unless-stopped \
  -e ADMIN_PASSWORD=<your-password> \
  -p 80:4179 \
  -v my-docs-data:/app/.docpilot-data \
  my-docs

Roadmap

  • WYSIWYG section editor (today: hand-authored HTML).
  • Per-doc public/private flags (today: per-tenant).
  • Branded PDF export from the published view.
  • Webhooks on publish + audit events.
Contribute back

Bug fixes and improvements welcome at github.com/EarendilM83/DocPilot/issues. The platform is content-agnostic by design; tenant data lives in your own deployment.
